text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Mubarak and Hussein talks in Aswan dealt with ways to push the peace process forward and the difficulties of implementing the Hebron agreement. The two leaders stressed the need to implement all agreements because not doing so would shake the foundations of peace.
- President Mubarak, in a humanitarian move, gives order for release of ailing Moslem Brotherhood man who was sentenced to three years in jail with hard labour for anti-government activities.

- Mubarak announces in historic celebration today the beginning of work in the project to develop the south Delta. President will send message to the world on development and will hold news conference at the end of the celebration.
- Suzanne Mubarak tells conference that next stage in development of Egypt will make use of women's abilities.
- Osama el-Baz says Egypt's relationship with U.S. is warm, honest and strong.
- Mubarak and Hussein visit High Dam and power station in Aswan.
- Chinese labour minister praises Egypt's economic reform programme and says Egypt will become an economic tiger.
- Work to start on Suez Canal bridge in May at cost of 500 million pounds; bridge will promote development of Sinai.
- Ramadan to start in 10 countries on Friday.
- Mubarak and Hussein tell news confernce in Aswan that there is no alternative to just and comprehensive peace and that the United States is a principle agent in the peace process.
- Ma'ariv's nonsense: Israeli paper quotes source as saying there is tension between Yasser Arafat and Egypt because Cairo is interfering in Hebron talks.
